record.title: Mali COVID land-passenger closure, March to July 2020 formal reopening
record.scope: National land-border passenger closure with freight exception
record.crossings: All national land frontiers in the policy; individual posts not exhaustively observed
record.direction: National land restriction; implementation and individual exceptions by direction not comprehensively documented.
record.movement: Ordinary passenger entry and exit through land borders.
record.exceptions: Freight and goods transport, especially essential supplies, explicitly exempt.
record.enforcement: Security ministry instructed forces to ensure closure; no claim of observation at every post.
record.consequences: Passenger access curtailed; no quantified border-specific impact adopted.
record.relationship: Precedes and is distinct from the August 2020 coup and ECOWAS restrictions W-009/W-010, and the 2022 sanctions W-011. Neighbour-imposed health restrictions may have continued beyond Mali’s repeal.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Containment of COVID-19 after the first confirmed cases.
record.context: Presidential address on 25 March announced the restriction; a 26 March security instruction ordered enforcement. A July decree separated land reopening from earlier air reopening.
record.uncertainty: 26 March onset is corroborated by AFP retrospective and contemporary enforcement instruction; exact first enforcement hour at land posts is not separately observed. July 31 is decree permission with health conditions, not a measured universal traffic restart.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. 26 March to 31 July is a policy chronology; no operational continuous duration calculated.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Ministry instruction and AFP retrospective support Mali land closure.
March 26 land closure distinguished from March 18 air closure; first hour at actual posts not measured.
July 31 at 00h is announced governmental permission; July 25 concerns air, not land.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): COVID rationale explicit.
Land passenger movement with essential-freight derogations; curfew 21h–05h is a separate measure.
Formal endpoints do not prove universal uninterrupted implementation or actual restoration.
